summary: Project ARES-5 is a game that aims to help players understand how much work the team behind these missions put into it and immersing those who would never be able to experience something like this in real life, simulate it here without any kind of setbacks. The game centers around a Martian mission and comprises of two chapters: planning the mission and executing it. This prototype encapsulates core gameplay elements, with many more expansions to add in the final game.
details:
Project ARES-5 is a simulation game where players have to execute an entire space mission by themselves.

Why?

So many of us have sat in front of the TV, watching the latest spacecraft, staring at the screen in awe and dreaming that we could be on the other side of that screen. Yet how many of us get the chance to realize that dream? Truth is, few people are lucky enough to even get close, but that's not fair.

On the other hand, the massive team behind these projects and the incredible amount of work they put into them go criminally underappreciated. Space missions are things of such a large scale that they become intangible to us. As such, we often forget that behind every small little thing we see are the fingerprints of real human beings. Thus, we end up forgetting to acknowledge these people.

That's precisely why this project was made: to shine a light on the people who lead humanity to the future and give those who dare to dream a breakthrough.

How it all works

The game consists of 2 parts:

  • Chapter 1: This is the planning section of the game. The players design their space mission by making choices about major components like the structural frame of the spacecraft, food supply for the journey, etc. They are given the pros and cons of each choice upfront; however, each choice has its own price and mass, and the player only has a limited budget and mass capacity, so they have to allocate their resources carefully. This is what ultimately decides the difficulty level of the game later on because each choice has a certain percentage chance of triggering an emergency onboard the spacecraft based on how difficult it is to manage vs. how efficient it is.
  • Chapter 2: This is the chapter where the main journey takes place. Players have to survive 5 days on the spacecraft while completing daily tasks, keeping their health meters filled (oxygen levels, temperature, and hunger) by eating and stabilizing oxygen and temperature, responding to spontaneous emergencies by figuring out emergency codes, and avoiding different external challenges thrown at them every day by following recovery protocols correctly.

If the players are successful, they will reach Mars, and if they fail, their progress instantly gets reset to the beginning of the game.

Dr. Axarian (our stand-in NPC) guides the player through the whole game, giving instructions and explaining everything to ensure that the only thing players have to worry about is having fun.

The Logistics

We put our hearts into making the game feel alive and used NASA data exclusively to actually bring it to life. The entire project was handcrafted by the development and creative subunits of this team, with some help from the following sources:

  • Gemini and ChatGPT were used to generate some background visuals for the UI.
  • Claude was used to help figure out how to debug certain codes. 
  • Figma was used to make the UI.
  • Godot was used to code the game (which was launched using itch.io)

Key Features of the game

  • Completely Free
  • Accessible on Windows, Apple, and Android.
  • Can be played offline.
  • Suitable for all ages.

The Prototype

While the project submitted is just a prototype for the full game, we ensured that it encapsulated the core mechanics of it. The extended version will have more aesthetic flourishes like an elaboration on the narrative story and cutscenes, as well as mechanical expansions like more challenges, tasks, and internal functions.

Aside from that, we also have plans for future developments such as a multiplayer mode, collectibles, and XP systems.

With enough time and a platform, the areas this game can reach are endless.

The Impact

Through Project ARES-5, we hope that players can not only learn how meticulously missions like these are planned from the very beginning, but also the weight of the responsibility the brave astronauts who go beyond the Earth shoulder.

The game forces players to think quickly, make on-spot decisions, stay calm under pressure, and manage everything all at once. There are no do-overs; every choice matters, and every little action decides whether their mission is a failure or success.

And for those who've spent years dreaming of reaching out towards the cosmos, Orbit Nexa is here.
